::: {#def-dfa}
#### Deterministic finite automaton (DFA)

A **deterministic finite automaton**, or **DFA**, [@wikipedia_deterministic_finite_automaton]
$M = (S, \Sigma, \delta, s_0, F)$ is a state machine $(S, \Sigma, \delta, s_0)$ (@def-state-machine)
together with a subset (@def-subset) $F \subseteq S$, whose elements are called *accepting states*.
Its state diagram is the state diagram (@def-state-diagram) of the state machine,
with each accepting state drawn as a double circle.

It is *deterministic* because each state and input give exactly one next state, $\delta(s, x)$.

:::
